Zero Company has, without a doubt, the potential to be one of the best games of the year and soon have new releases being compared to it, not the other way around.

Zero Company's production values are…intense.

This is easily one of the best-looking games on the market and the authenticity to the Star Wars brand is both impressive and super immersive.

It has all the bells and whistles, really. The powerhouse graphics look great, the sound design is splendid, the ambiance and overall soundtrack is exactly what it needs to be for the brand and the overall package is exactly what one would dream up when thinking about a Star Wars themed XCOM.

Indeed, Zero Company isn't trying to duck comparisons with its gameplay. Rather, it's trying to layer atop the tried-and-true stuff.

The cover system is there. Full cover is a 50 percent penalty. Flanking leads to exposure states. Certain cover can be destroyed. There's an overwatch system to make characters auto-shoot opponents that enter the zone. Action points per turn govern, well, actions.

And yes, the hallmark of the genre, missing on a shot that has a 90 percent chance to hit? It's there.

Interesting layerings on the formula include being able to call for backup once per turn, assisting attacks. There are ultimate abilities, too, charged through an "advantage" point system shared by all friendly characters that increases by attacking enemies.

These ultimate abilities range from massive things like a rocket launcher attack to less costly, little strategy nuance, such as the ability to refresh a squadmate's AP for that turn.

Different primary weapons define each type of character capable of being added to squads.

Each character, too can equip a certain amount of utilities, talents and specializations.

Specializations won't shock those familiar with XCOM games and similar. Characters can go full-blown assault, the tank-like heavy class, medic, and so on.

Speaking of character and squad makeup, there are stakes. Characters getting defeated rack up injuries. A third injury means permadeath for a character, so players must carefully manage things not just in battle, but post-and-pre battle, too. Except for the main character, anyway, that just leads to a game-over.

Impressive depth and teambuilding strategies here too, no doubt. There's no restriction on pairing certain primary weapons with certain specializations. Weapons being moddable, too, is one of the many things that will lead to unique player-to-player builds that can change for a variety of different encounters.

Mission structures get a nice mixup too. Side missions are standard things like rescue missions or hold-the-area waves. But story missions can have multiple stages with some exploration and storytelling phases to break up the action.

Zero Company hits on some of the best story beats and characters the Star Wars universe has offered in years.

Players assume the role of Hawks, the leader of the game's namesake, "Zero Company." There's a rebellious nature to it all, and baddies to fight and the narrative does a good job of looping in the many different types of enemies and characters documented in a way that makes sense.

Beyond the narrative, managing the "Den" is similar to a variety of games. There's always a ton to do, to the point it might turn some players away because they just want to get back into the fights. Others, though, will appreciate the depth and the sense of immersion it provides in terms of really feeling in command of a multi-layered organization.

The hub does some of the basic stuff players would expect. Players can recruit new members and outfit their squads, among other things.

There are little side missions too that can be largely text-based. It's immersive to pop into the operations center and make key strategic decisions for in-progress, off-screen missions, even if they're simple text-based experiences.

Perhaps a refreshing twist on the concept, at least for similar strategy games, is being able to put boots on the ground and go around talking to characters. It's a fun wrinkle similar to old Star Wars classics like Knights of the OId Republic, which can help players care about the characters they're sending into battle more than usual.

Along the way, Zero Company runs well and has the expected suite of options within the solid UI.

Zero Company sort of snuck up on the gaming calendar this year. A tactical RPG in the XCOM mold with Star Wars window dressing was a little easy to overlook.

There's a great Star Wars tale here and the combination of the source material and genre is a no-brainer in a way Gears War Tactics or Midnight Suns were years ago. The gameplay is a chef's kiss balance between pick-up-and-play approachable and where-did-the-hours-go strategic.

Not bad for Zero Company, really, a bit of an underdog story that now lands as a serious Game of the Year contender.

articles.title: Exclusive: LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight Deluxe Edition - Mayhem Collection DLC Trailer Reveals The Joker and Harley Quinn Story Mission and More
articles.summary: During our IGN gamescom Studio livestream, we were able to exclusively reveal the LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight Deluxe Edition - Mayhem Collection DLC trailer, which features an exciting look at the new story mission starring Harley Quinn and the Joker, the Mayhem Mode, and the Sinister Pack.
articles.body:
During the gamescom Studio livestream, IGN exclusively revealed the trailer for LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight Deluxe Edition - Mayhem Collection DLC, which features an exciting look at the new story mission starring Harley Quinn and The Joker, the Mayhem Mode, and the Sinister Pack.

LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight's Mayhem Collection DLC will be available to all Deluxe Edition owners for no extra cost on September 18, 2026, which also happens to be the same day the game launches on Nintendo Switch 2.

The big addition in the DLC is that new story mission that stars Harley Quinn and The Joker, which will see the pair working together to "orchestrate a breakout from Arkham Asylum with a going-away party Gotham City won't soon forget."

Harley Quinn will be equipped with her trusty hammer and her Fun Gun loaded with Confetti and Bubblegum, and she'll also be able to summon her beloved hyenas, Bud & Lou. As for The Joker, he'll bring his Paintball Pelter and Boxing Glove to the party alongside a "fast-paced, agile combat style that is focused on speed and mobility." Players will also be able to unlock outfits for Harley Quinn and The Joker that are based on past Batman Media, including The Dark Knight Returns comic book series, Batman: The Animated Series, and more.

Outside of the story, the Mayhem Mode will unleash Harley Quinn and The Joker across Gotham City and task them with time-limited Mayhem Runs. During each run, they will need to make it back to Amusement Mile before time runs out, and they will be chased by Batman and Robin while doing so. You'll earn LEGO studs by smashing everything in sight and completing challenges, alongside battling A.R.G.U.S. Agents and members of Amanda Waller's Task Force X in Deathstroke, Killer Croc, Captain Boomerang, Deadshot, King Shark, Polka-Dot Man, and other "notorious DC Super-Villains."

LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight - Mayhem Collection DLC Images

The Sinister Pack includes themed outfits inspired by popular DC comic book issues and action figures, plus a new vehicle and Batcave customization options. The full list of items this pack includes is as follows:

Batman – The Batman Who Laughs outfit (Dark Nights: Metal #2 | 2017)

Robin – Robin King outfit (Dark Nights: DM – Legends of the Dark Knights #1 | 2020)

Nightwing – Joker outfit (Nightwing #16 | 2011)

Batgirl – Joker outfit (Jokerized DC Multiverse Action Figure)

Jim Gordon – Joker outfit (The Joker: The Man Who Stopped Laughing #9 | 2022)

Catwoman – Joker outfit (Catwoman #65 | 1993)

Talia al Ghul – Joker (Earth-37) outfit (DC Elseworlds comic series | 1997)

Batcave Items – Helmet (The Merciless), Joker Fish Aquarium, Barbatos Statue, Snake Clowns, and Long Halloween Pumpkin

The last thing that will be added on September 18 will be an enhanced 'Absolute' difficulty level, which will actually be a free update for all players. This new difficulty mode will require "greater skill, awareness, and precision in combat."

LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight released on PS5, Xbox Series X/S, and PC back in May 2026, and in our review, we said, "a strong open-world Gotham and trademark Lego slapstick humour powers a fantastic plastic parody of Batman’s greatest hits."

Adam Bankhurst is a writer for IGN. You can follow him on X/Twitter @AdamBankhurst, Instagram, and TikTok, and listen to his show, Talking Disney Magic.

articles.title: Xbox announces disc-to-digital feature that digitizes your physical games
articles.summary: Microsoft is launching a new Xbox feature to digitize Xbox discs. Xbox owners will be able to turn their physical game collections into digital ones.
articles.body: Microsoft is officially announcing a new Xbox feature that will allow Xbox owners to digitize their existing physical game collections. The disc-to-digital feature, which The Verge exclusively revealed last month, is part of work that Microsoft is doing for game preservation and in preparation for the next generation of Xbox consoles. “Most Xbox One and Xbox Series X disc-based games support this new feature,” explains Jason Ronald, VP of next generation at Xbox. “Players can claim a digital entitlement by inserting a supported disc into an Xbox One or Xbox Series X console and launching the game.” This digital entitlement is tied to the specific disc, and it will move from account to account if you swap the physical game with a friend or log in to a different Xbox profile and try to play a disc-based game. Microsoft will start testing this new Xbox disc-to-digital feature with Xbox Insider testers on August 31st, followed by a broader rollout to Xbox One and Xbox Series X consoles in the coming months. Once you have a digital version of an Xbox disc game, if supported you’ll also be able to access the game on PC through Xbox Play Anywhere, or stream it to multiple devices with Xbox Cloud Gaming. A leaked memo from earlier this month revealed that publishers would have control over the Xbox disc-to-digital, so not every game will be supported initially. “We’re starting with thousands of titles, and we’ll continue to add more over time,” says Ronald. “While not every title will be available at launch, this is an important step toward a future where players can have greater confidence that the games they buy remain with them for years to come.” The Xbox disc-to-digital feature arrives just weeks after Sony announced it’s killing all physical PlayStation game discs. New PlayStation games released after January 2028 will be digital-only, but it’s not yet clear if Microsoft will announce a similar end of production for Xbox discs. Either way, Sony hasn’t announced a similar feature for converting an existing physical library into a digital one. Microsoft is also bringing Xbox and Xbox 360 games to PC, in a move that could allow the next Xbox console to play every Xbox game ever made.

articles.title: Xbox Wireless Controller X25 Special Edition Preorders Are Live
articles.summary: You can now preorder the Xbox Wireless Controller X25 Special Edition from a variety of retailers.
articles.body:
The Xbox Wireless Controller X25 Special Edition is now available for preorder at Walmart , Best Buy and the Microsoft Store . It’s a striking translucent green controller, with numerous features that call back to the original Xbox console. It costs $79.99 and will release on October 20.

Preorder XBOX Wireless Controller X25 Special Edition

XBOX Wireless Controller X25 Special Edition

The translucent green looks fantastic, if you ask me. The Xbox button in the top center of the controller glows green in a nod to what the company says is "the first green X bursting through," presumably in the Xbox's startup animation . On the battery cover on the back of the controller is the original Xbox logo.

The left and right bumpers are white and black, respectively, which call to mind the extra face buttons on the original Xbox controller. Speaking of the face buttons, they're colored green, red, yellow, and blue, just like on the original.

But it's not all retro-styling on this controller. The triggers and bumpers are textured for better grip and less slippage. It also has all the other features you'd expect on a modern Xbox controller, like wireless connectivity and wide compatibility with Windows, Mac, and mobile.

Microsoft is busy with announcements during Gamescom , including the ability to digitize your physical games , starting next week.

articles.title: Xbox's 25th Anniversary Limited Edition Console Price and Release Date Revealed, Comes With Halo: Campaign Evolved
articles.summary: Xbox has revealed the price and release date for its 25th anniversary limited edition console, and it comes with a free game too.
articles.body:
Xbox has revealed the price and release date for its 25th anniversary limited edition console, and it comes with a free game too.

Earlier this summer, Microsoft revealed that it will be releasing a translucent green Xbox Series X console , inspired by the original Xbox console, for the company's 25th anniversary. Now, Microsoft has confirmed that the console will cost a whopping $899.99 and release on November 13. It will come with the Xbox Series X console, a matching controller, and a free copy of Halo: Campaign Evolved. Pre-orders will open tomorrow, August 27, at 7 AM PDT.

The controller can be purchased separately for $79.99, and it will release on October 20. If you're in the market for a brand new Xbox, this isn't a bad deal. The Xbox Series X itself costs $799.99 with a disc drive. This costs an extra $100 and includes one of Xbox's biggest games of the year. However, the next-generation of Xbox is also likely right around the corner. Microsoft confirmed earlier this year that it will detail its next console, codenamed Project Helix, later this year.

It wouldn't be surprising if the next Xbox releases in fall 2027, as Microsoft has already indicated that will be a really important window for the company . The company also unveiled plans for a new disc-to-digital feature that will allow users to get a digital copy of their physical Xbox One and Xbox Series X games. It's been speculated that this is to prepare players for a transition to a more digital-focused next-generation console.
